Subject: Acme trial — procurement & billing readiness

Hi Alicia,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to meet you and the team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on the trial -> paid path: 

Call recap (very short):
- Trial scope: 3 internal teams (Search, Support, Summaries) using the Redwood hosted inference endpoints.
- Success criteria: 70% reduction in average support response time for the pilot team, acceptable latency under 350ms p95, and stable cost per 1k tokens within the forecast.
- Timeline: 6-week trial starting this week for onboarding + evaluation.

Procurement & commercial path items:
1) Payment method — can Acme accept card for initial subscription or will you need to go through a Purchase Order (PO)? If PO, please confirm the billing contact and approximate procurement lead time.
2) Marketplace — you mentioned AWS Marketplace as an option. Do you prefer transacting through marketplace (we can publish a listing / provide marketplace invoice) or direct with Redwood?
3) Billing start — do you want billing to start immediately after trial activation, or on a trigger (e.g., hitting a usage threshold or a mutually agreed date)?
4) Trial guardrails — I attached a short MRAP and a PO template for your procurement/finance team to review.

Next steps I propose:
- Alicia: confirm procurement path (card vs PO vs marketplace) and share procurement contact (cc'd procurement@acme.com is fine).
- Rajiv / Procurement: if PO, please review the attached purchase_order_template.pdf and advise on any required terms.
- Redwood: we'll send a formal quote/SOW and can set a soft billing start date (we typically set billing to start when trial usage exceeds agreed thresholds or on a calendar date — happy to align with you).

Happy to hop on a 15-min call with procurement if that speeds things up.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — that matches our notes. A few quick answers from procurement side: 

- Payment method: Acme prefers a PO for anything over $10k. For initial PoC spend under $10k we can do a corporate card, but the procurement team will still need the PO paperwork if we intend to commit to a longer term/production contract.
- Procurement contact: Looping in Rajiv (VP, Procurement) and our procurement email. Rajiv, can you confirm typical lead time and whether Net30 is acceptable?
- Marketplace: We prefer AWS Marketplace where possible because it simplifies internal billing. If you have an existing listing or can enable marketplace invoicing, we'd prefer that route.
- Billing start: We want billing to start when the trial crosses the pilot success threshold (we'll confirm the exact metric after week 2), not immediately.

A couple of asks: can you provide the expected monthly spend at different usage bands (e.g., 0-50M tokens / 50-200M tokens / 200M+ tokens) so procurement can justify the spend bands? Also please confirm whether Redwood supports marketplace invoicing and whether PO paperwork is compatible with marketplace purchases.

Thanks — happy to set a short call with Rajiv and procurement next week to close this out.

Best,
Alicia

Hi Alicia / Marissa,

Quick technical note from the SE side to help with the usage bands and billing trigger question: 

- Typical trial behavior: initial spike during integration (first week) then plateau. For the workloads you described (search + support + summaries) we estimate:
  - Low: 0-50M tokens/mo — light usage, mainly dev and early pilot users
  - Mid: 50-200M tokens/mo — active pilot, production-like traffic for a subset of users
  - High: 200M+ tokens/mo — broad rollout across teams

- Cost estimate (hosted Redwood public pricing examples; final quote will reflect reserved rates if you go Dedicated):
  - 0-50M tokens: ~$1,200-~$3,000 / month
  - 50-200M tokens: ~$3,000-~$10,000 / month
  - 200M+: contact for tailored reserved capacity pricing

- Billing triggers: we recommend one of the following for trial -> paid transition:
  1) Usage trigger: billing starts when cumulative trial usage exceeds 50M tokens, OR
  2) Date trigger: billing starts on a mutually agreed calendar date (e.g., 2026-09-01), OR
  3) Success trigger: billing starts when the pilot meets agreed success criteria (latency + accuracy + adoption).

Marketplace notes: we support AWS Marketplace invoicing for SaaS and for metered billing, but POs are less straightforward via marketplace — typically procurement will handle the marketplace purchase and invoice flow, which removes the need for a Redwood-issued PO. If procurement needs a Redwood invoice and PO, we can do direct invoicing instead.

I've attached a short sample usage-to-cost spreadsheet (trial-success-criteria.xlsx) and a one-pager with typical thresholds. Happy to refine numbers after we get a sense of expected concurrent users.

Vivek
